issues.title: Define the scope and the list of target events
issues.author: huitema
issues.body:
The first requirement for this TLS draft is to define the scope. My preference would be to look at the TLS API used by QUIC, and list the events that we want to log. we know about 2 of them, SNI selection and ALPN selection, but there are probably more. Things like sucess/failure, HRR, 0RTT negotiated or not, ECH.

Also, probably, some logging of the TLS tickets.

comments.author: huitema
comments.body:
From various discussions:

* ALPN information: there is consensus to move the definition from the QUIC to the TLS name space.

* SNI: there is consensus that we should log it.

* from [qlog issue 121](https://github.com/quicwg/qlog/issues/121):  log the QUIC-accessible part of the session resume ticket.

* from picoquic experience: log whether a session ticket is available, whether the connection was resumed, whether 0-RTT was supported. This is also mentioned in [qlog issue 27](https://github.com/quicwg/qlog/issues/27)

* log whether a session establishment failed, and try to log the reason.

* consider logging whether ECH was tried, and then whether it was negotiated

comments.author: toidiu
comments.body:
This is a great list. 

A few things we were speaking about offline.Nothing set in stone and @huitema please feel free to correct me.
- We will only support TLS 1.3
- We need to support events emitted from both H3 and H2 connections
- @huitema you mentioned in slack that we should limit the events to "TLS 1.3 at the granularity of what is visible by the app". Can you expand on this. Its nice to have detailed info about the TLS handshake for debugging purposes and metrics but these would not necessarily be available to the app. 

Some other fields that came to mind:
- tls params that were chosen for the connection
  - cipher suites
  - key exchange group
  - meta info about the cert? (for example to debug if PQ schemes were negotiated)
- mTLS
- session resumption and 0-rtt (its nice to have [reason](https://commondatastorage.googleapis.com/chromium-boringssl-docs/ssl.h.html#ssl_early_data_reason_t) why the session was not resumed but we should be impl agnostic)

comments.author: huitema
comments.body: We do qlog to get a structured log of a networking application. We might for example log an H3 application, and for that we can use qlog specs for H3 and QUIC. That's practical because the H3 and QUIC are usually developed as part of related software libraries. Those libraries have to interface with TLS 1.3 to get keys, check certs, etc. That means we have good chance of logging the "interface" interactions between the H3 or QUIC and TLS 1.3. But the application does not usually have access to the internals of the TLS implementation -- that's done inside OpenSSL or other libraries, and I don't think we can realistically ask these libraries to do qlog.

comments.author: huitema
comments.body:
"session resumption and 0-rtt (its nice to have [reason](https://commondatastorage.googleapis.com/chromium-boringssl-docs/ssl.h.html#ssl_early_data_reason_t) why the session was not resumed but we should be impl agnostic)": the way we do that is we define an event with mandatory elements such as accepted/refused, resumed or not, 0RTT or not; and we also define optional elements that provide more information if available. 

See for example the definition of a token (QUIC level) in the QUIC qlog events draft:
```
Token = {
    ? type: $TokenType

    ; decoded fields included in the token
    ; (typically: peer's IP address, creation time)
    ? details: {
      * text => any
    }
    ? raw: RawInfo

    * $$quic-token-extension
}

$TokenType /= "retry" /
              "resumption"
```

comments.author: huitema
comments.body:
This is an extract of the console output of a picoquic connection, complemented by information logged at the server. I removed the report lines that relate to QUIC and H3:

First lines indicate that the client will use a session resume ticket, set the ALPN and QUIC version to the values associated with that ticket:
~~~
Starting Picoquic (v1.1.54.0) connection to server = test.privateoctopus.com, port = 4433
Set ALPN to h3 based on stored ticket
Set version to 0x00000001 based on stored ticket
~~~

This could be extended into a "TLSSessionStart" at client. Maybe a similar log on the server side. The server side qlog display some data as information message:
~~~
[174, 0, "transport", "parameters_set", {
    "owner": "remote",
    "sni": "test.privateoctopus.com",
    "proposed_alpn": ["h3"],
    "alpn": "h3"}],
[193, 0, "info", "message", { "message": "Session ticket properly decrypted"}],
~~~
This kind of info could be added to an event, "TLSSessionRequested" (by a client), although we may also want to document ALPN negotiation in its own event. We could discuss whether the client and server side of these events should be a single event with parameters, or two events.

We can track the progress of the session by looking at the qlog, showing "initial" and "handshake" packets, and the carrying of TLS data in "crypto" frames. If you have good eyes, you can see that one of the "handshake" packets received from the client carries a "crypto" frame:
~~~
[118794, 0, "transport", "packet_received", { "packet_type": "handshake", "header": { "packet_size": 93, "packet_number": 0, "payload_length": 48, "scid": "9274864ce2165713", "dcid": "c9dcb5a670f871bc" }, "frames": [{ 
    "frame_type": "ack", "ack_delay": 99, "acked_ranges": [[0, 1]], "ect0": 2, "ect1": 0, "ce": 0}, { 
    "frame_type": "crypto", "offset": 0, "length": 36}]}],
~~~
This contains the "client finished" message. Might be good to log that in an event, "TLSSessionComplete". We may want to add additional negotiation, such as the negotiated Crypto suite.

On the client UI, results of connection show that in that case the session was accepted, the resumption was successful, zero RTT data was supported.
~~~
The session was properly resumed!
Zero RTT data is accepted!
Negotiated ALPN: h3
~~~
Again, this look like information that could fit in a "TLSSessionComplete". event. Note that in the picoquic case the transport code does not see the certificate, it is all handled inside the TLS stack.

The session executes. At the end, the UI prints some statistics, and details about the session resume ticket that was received. we do not show here the 137 bytes of the actual ticket, only the information that is available to the client:
~~~
Received ticket from test.privateoctopus.com (h3):
ticket time = 1795564417938, kx = 1d, suite = 1301, 137 ticket, 32 secret.
lifetime = 100000, age_add = a71e4232, 0 nonce, 116 ticket, 8 extensions.
ticket extensions: 42(ED: ffffffff),
Client exit with code = 0
~~~
This would map neastly to a TLSResumeTicketReceived event.

comments.author: huitema
comments.body:
Purposely starting a connection with the wrong ALPN.

On the server's qlog, we see the incoming request:
~~~
[182, 0, "transport", "parameters_set", {
    "owner": "remote",
    "sni": "test.privateoctopus.com",
    "proposed_alpn": ["bad_alpn"]}],
~~~

We also see that the alpn is wrong, but don't have a structured error message for that. Instead, we have informal traces:
~~~
[184, 0, "info", "message", { "message": "Client Hello call back returns 120 (0x78)"}],
[186, 0, "info", "message", { "message": "Picotls returns error: 120 (0x78)"}],
[187, 0, "info", "message", { "message": "Protocol error 0x178, frame 0, reason: ?"}],
~~~

QUIC Error 0x178 is TLS alert 120 (0x78): no_application_protocol. We may want to log TLS alerts in either a "TLSSessionRefused" event or a TLSAlert event.

The client UI similarly says:
~~~
The connection is closed!
Connection ends with remote error 0x178 (wrong alpn).
~~~

But then, the connection error is also logged at the QUIC level, and it could log the TLS error code explicitly.
